Agencies Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities , according to the Bharat InvITs Association . Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. Investcorp-backed NDR InvIT Trust is also planning to transition into a public InvIT through an issue of up to Rs 750 crore, while KKR and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP)-sponsored Vertis Infrastructure Trust is also exploring an IPO. In March, NHAI-sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust raised Rs 6,000 crore through its IPO. Live Events The growing pipeline of public offerings comes amid an expansion in India's InvIT market, estimated at around Rs 7.5 lakh crore, as infrastructure companies increasingly look at the trust structure to unlock capital from operational assets and fund future expansion . The market is also attracting a wider pool of investors. InvITs had around 6.5 lakh unitholders as of the first quarter of FY27, and over the past 10 years, InvITs have collectively distributed nearly Rs 1 lakh crore to their investors, as per the Bharat InvITs Association. Under SEBI regulations, InvITs are required to distribute at least 90 per cent of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders, making them an attractive investment avenue for investors seeking regular income. The investor base is also gradually broadening, with a growing number of women participating as unitholders, according to brokers and wealth advisers. The sector has received a further boost from the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) introduction of a framework for depository receipts, allowing foreign investors to gain exposure to Indian REITs and InvITs through select overseas exchanges. Reliance Brands Ltd (RBL), a subsidiary of the country's leading retailer Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL), operates business of global fashion and lifestyle brands in India market through strategic partnerships, brand ownership and retail operations . RBL reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,267.66 crore and a profit of Rs 237.12 crore in FY25, according to financial data accessed through the business intelligence platform Tofler. It manages a diverse and expanding portfolio of international and domestic brands across luxury, bridge-to-luxury, premium, and high-street fashion, as well as F&B, eyewear, home & lifestyle, and toys. It entered into master franchise partnerships with contemporary womenswear brands Stella McCartney and MAX&Co, as well as British luxury footwear and accessories brand Kurt Geiger, thereby enhancing its presence across premium fashion segments. The company also expanded into the high-growth athleisure and activewear category through a master franchise partnership with Fabletics, launching a new portfolio vertical and reinforcing its commitment to capturing evolving consumer lifestyle trends. "During the year under review, your company achieved a net turnover of Rs 3,390.89 crore as compared to Rs 3,267.66 crore during last year. The rupee closed at 92.91 per dollar, down 0.26% from its close at 92.67 in the previous session. While the South Asian currency had perked up to a high of 92.44 in early trading - its strongest level since April - it turned lower afterwards, with traders pointing to strong importer dollar demand, including from two large conglomerates. Weakness in local stocks also became a sentiment drag on the unit, with the benchmark Nifty 50 down nearly 2% after touching its highest level since February earlier in the day. Indian equities and the rupee have been regional outperformers in November so far as worries over crowded global AI trades drew over $10 billion of foreign investor money.
